title: Asking and Answering
overview: Ask people questions with do and does. Answer: Yes, I do. No, I don't. Write I'm, don't, doesn't and isn't. Ask: How do you spell that? Say your job and where you live.
learningPath: Words: listen, look and say. 24 words.
Patterns: 4 cards. Read the one done for you.
Reading: read the 3 texts. Answer the questions.
Speaking: tap the mic. Say it. Listen.
Writing: write about you. Made-up details are OK.
Practice: write. Check with the answers.
lectureScript:
Hello! This is Unit 7.
In this unit, you ask people questions. And you answer.
Listen.
Hello. I'm Lena. I'm a nurse.
Do you live here?
Yes, I do. I live at number 8.
Nice to meet you.
First, questions with do and does.
Use do with I, you, we and they.
Do you work? Do they know Omar?
Use does with he, she and it.
Does she work? Does he live here?
A question word can go first.
Where do you live? Where does she work?
After does, the next word has no s.
Not: Where does she works? Say: Where does she work?
In the answer, the s comes back.
Where does she work? She works in a shop.
Now short answers.
Do you live here? Yes, I do. No, I don't.
Does he drive a bus? Yes, he does. No, he doesn't.
The question has do? Say do again.
The question has does? Say does again.
Now short forms. Two words make one.
I am: I'm.
Do not: don't.
Does not: doesn't.
Is not: isn't.
I'm a student.
I don't work on Sunday.
She doesn't live in a city.
He isn't a doctor.
Now three new question words.
When asks for a time or a day.
When do you work? On Monday.
Why asks for a reason.
Why do you study English? For my job.
Which asks you to choose.
Which bus is it? Bus 6.
Now a question for anyone.
How do you spell that?
Here, you means any person. Not only you.
How do you say this word?
What do you call this in English?
Listen.
What is your surname?
Dale.
How do you spell that?
D-A-L-E.
Now jobs. Listen and repeat.
Doctor. Nurse. Teacher. Driver. Farmer.
Student. Shopkeeper. Police officer. Cleaner.
What is your job? I'm a cleaner.
Do you study? Yes, I do. I'm a student.
Say your job, or a job you know. A made-up job is OK.
Last, your details.
Your address: a number and a street. 12 Park Street.
Your surname: your family name.
Your phone number: say it one number at a time.
Do you live in a city or a village?
Which country are you from?
You can use made-up details.
Now go to Words. Goodbye!

outcomes.evidence: Pattern 2 practice; Practice 2, eight items; Speaking 2 recording; Writing 2 checklist; Reading 1 question 2; Quiz items 3 to 5.
outcomes.cefrDescriptor: I can answer: Yes, I do. No, I don't.

outcomes.evidence: Pattern 3 practice; Practice 3, eight items; Speaking 3 recording; Writing 3 checklist; Quiz items 6 and 7.
outcomes.cefrDescriptor: I can write I'm, don't, doesn't and isn't.

words.meaning: The work you do. Doctor, driver and cleaner are jobs.
practice: My job is in an office.
I don't have a job. I'm a student.
Do you like your job?
Her job is at a school.
What is his job? He is a driver.
words.tutor: Tell the tutor a made-up job, or a job you know. Then ask it What is your job? and check its answer starts with I'm a.

words.meaning: A person who helps ill people.
practice: The doctor works at night.
Is he a doctor? Yes, he is.
Where does the doctor work?
Does the doctor work on Sunday?
words.tutor: Make up a doctor. Ask the tutor three does questions about her. Like this: Does she work on Sunday? Check: no s after does.

words.meaning: A person who helps ill people and helps a doctor.
practice: A nurse helps the doctor.
Is she a nurse? No, she isn't.
The nurse works in the evening.
Does your brother work as a nurse?
words.tutor: Say two things a nurse does. Like this: A nurse helps ill people. Ask the tutor for one more. Say it back.

words.meaning: A person at a school who helps people study.
words.example: He is a teacher at a big school.
practice: Is she a teacher? Yes, she is.
My aunt is a teacher.
Where does the teacher work?
A teacher works with students.
words.tutor: Make up a teacher. Ask the tutor Does a teacher work on Saturday? Then answer two does questions about your made-up teacher.

words.meaning: A person who drives a bus, for work.
practice: Is he a driver? Yes, he is.
The driver stops the bus.
My father is a driver.
When does the driver work?
words.tutor: Make up a bus driver. Tell the tutor which bus, and when. Like this: She drives bus 6 in the morning.

words.meaning: A person who grows food and keeps animals.
practice: Does the farmer live in a village? Yes, he does.
Farmers work in the morning.
Is she a farmer? No, she isn't.
A farmer works with animals.
words.tutor: Ask the tutor: Where does a farmer work? Listen. Then say the answer back, with works.

words.meaning: A person who studies, like you with English.
practice: Are you a student? Yes, I am.
She is a student and a nurse.
The students are in Room 3.
Is he a student? No, he isn't.
words.tutor: Tell the tutor: I'm a student of … and one thing you study. Let it ask: When do you study? Answer with a day or a time.

words.meaning: A person with a small shop, who works in it.
words.example: The shopkeeper opens the shop at eight o'clock.
practice: Is she a shopkeeper? Yes, she is.
The shopkeeper knows my name.
Our neighbour is a shopkeeper.
Where does the shopkeeper live?
words.tutor: Make up a shopkeeper. Tell the tutor when the shop opens and closes. Like this: It opens at eight o'clock.

words.meaning: A person who keeps people safe on the street.
words.example: The police officer helps a woman on the street.
practice: Is he a police officer?
Ask a police officer for help.
My cousin is a police officer.
Police officers work day and night.
words.tutor: Say police officer slowly, then fast, as two words: po-LICE OF-fi-cer. Ask the tutor: are both words clear?

words.meaning: A person who cleans rooms, offices or streets, for work.
words.example: The cleaner works in an office.
practice: Is she a cleaner? Yes, she is.
The cleaner comes in the evening.
Does the cleaner work on Saturday?
My neighbour is a cleaner at a school.
words.tutor: Tell the tutor what a cleaner cleans, and when. Like this: The cleaner cleans the office at six o'clock. Check: cleans, with an s.

words.meaning: It asks for a time or a day.
words.example: When do you work? On Monday.
practice: When does the shop open? At nine o'clock.
When do you study?
When do they meet? On Friday.
When does she sleep? In the morning.
words.tutor: Ask the tutor three when questions about its made-up day. Check that each answer is a time or a day.

words.meaning: It asks for a reason. The answer can start with for.
words.example: Why do you study English? For my job.
practice: Why does he work at night? He is a nurse.
Why do you ask?
Why are you here? For a new card.
Why do they walk? The bus is full.
words.tutor: Ask the tutor: Why do you study English? Then answer it yourself. Use for, like this: For my job.

words.meaning: It asks you to choose, from two or more.
practice: Which bag is your bag? The red bag.
Which day do you work?
Which street do you live on?
Which door is it? The blue door.
words.tutor: Ask the tutor for two choices, like bus 6 or bus 10. Ask a which question about them. Then answer it.

words.meaning: The number and the street of your home.
practice: What is your address?
Write your address here, please.
Does she know your address?
Our address is 7 Garden Street.
words.tutor: Say a made-up address: a number from 1 to 20 and a street. Ask the tutor to write it. Check it.

words.meaning: Your family name. It comes after your first name.
practice: What is your surname?
How do you spell your surname?
Her first name is Eva. Her surname is Hart.
Write your surname in capital letters.
words.tutor: Say a made-up first name and surname. Spell the surname, letter by letter. Ask the tutor to write it. Check the letters.

words.meaning: Words like two and ten. A phone and a house have one too.
practice: My house number is 9.
Say the number again, please.
Which number is your house?
Write the number in words.
words.tutor: Say a made-up phone number to the tutor. Say one number at a time. Ask it to say the number back. Check each one.

words.meaning: A very big town, with lots of streets, shops and people.
words.example: I live in a big city.
practice: Do you live in a city?
The city has many parks.
My cousin works in the city.
Which city do you live in?
words.starter: I live in a city. It is …
words.tutor: Tell the tutor two things about a city. Then ask it: Do you live in a city? Listen to its short answer.

words.meaning: A very small place, with one or two streets.
words.example: My grandmother lives in a village.
practice: Do you live in a city or a village?
The village has one shop.
Many farmers live in the village.
Our village is small and green.
words.tutor: Make up a village. Say three lines about it: a shop, a street, a job. Then say three lines about a city.

words.meaning: A big land with its own name. It has cities and villages.
practice: My country has big cities.
What is the name of your country?
English is a language in many countries.
Many people live in this country.
words.starter: I am from a country with …
words.tutor: Say where you are from. You can use a made-up country. Then ask the tutor Which country are you from? and check its answer uses from.

words.meaning: A person who lives next to you or near you.
practice: Do you know your neighbours?
Our neighbour lives at number 7.
Say hello to your neighbour.
My neighbour doesn't work on Sunday.
words.tutor: Make up a neighbour. Tell the tutor three things with does or doesn't. Like this: She doesn't work on Sunday.

words.meaning: It is in your head, and you can say it.
practice: Do you know the answer?
Sorry, I don't know.
Does she know Omar? Yes, she does.
We know our neighbours.
words.tutor: Ask the tutor: Do you know …? Ask about three words from this unit. Then it asks you. Answer: Yes, I do. Or: No, I don't.

words.meaning: To see a person, often for the first time.
practice: I meet my friend on Saturday.
Where do you meet?
When do they meet? In the evening.
Hello, I'm Ben. Nice to meet you.
words.tutor: Role-play with the tutor: you meet for the first time. Say hello, a made-up name and Nice to meet you.

words.meaning: To say a question to a person.
words.example: Ask the driver: Which bus is it?
practice: Ask the person at the desk.
Why do you ask?
I ask, and you answer.
She asks: Where do you live?
words.tutor: Ask the tutor five questions about its made-up job. Use what, where, when, why and which. Check each one ends with a question mark.

words.meaning: To say or write back when a person asks.
practice: What is the answer?
I know the answer!
She doesn't answer her phone.
Answer in English, please.
words.tutor: Ask the tutor for five do and does questions. Answer each one with a short answer. Then answer with a full line.

grammar.title: Asking with do and does
grammar.explanation:
Many questions start with do or does.
I, you, we, they: do.
He, she, it: does.
After does, the next word has no s.
grammar.rule:
do: I, you, we, they
Do you live here?
Do they work on Monday?
Where do you work?

does: he, she, it
Does she live here?
Does Omar speak English?
Where does she work?

A question word goes first:
When does the shop open?
Why do you study English?
Which day do you work?
grammar.workedExample:
Mia / work / in a shop. Make a question.
1. Mia is a woman: she.
2. She goes with does.
3. Does goes first. Then Mia.
4. Then work, with no s.
5. Does Mia work in a shop?
6. Check: does, and no s on work. Yes.
grammar.mistake:
It is easy to keep the s after does.
No: Where does she works?
Yes: Where does she work?
Does has the s. The next word has none.
In the answer, the s comes back.
She works in a shop.
grammar.tip: Does takes the s. The next word does not.
grammar.practice:
Write do or does.
1. ___ you live here?
2. Where ___ she work?
3. ___ they speak English?
4. When ___ he study?
5. ___ your brother drive a bus?
6. Which day ___ you work?
7. Why ___ Omar walk to work?
8. ___ we know the answer?
grammar.answers:
1. Do  2. does  3. Do  4. does  5. Does  6. do  7. does  8. Do
Wrong on 5? Your brother is one man: he. He goes with does.
Wrong on 7? Omar is one name: he. So does.

grammar.title: Yes, I do. No, she doesn't.
grammar.explanation:
Answer with yes or no.
Then the person, then do or does.
The question has is? The answer has is.
grammar.rule:
Do you live here?
Yes, I do.
No, I don't.

Do they know Ana?
Yes, they do.
No, they don't.

Does she work here?
Yes, she does.
No, she doesn't.

Does he drive a bus?
Yes, he does.
No, he doesn't.

Is she a nurse?
Yes, she is.
grammar.workedExample:
Does Priya live in a city?
Priya lives in a village.
1. The question starts with does.
2. She lives in a village. So the answer is no.
3. Priya is a woman: she.
4. No, she doesn't.
grammar.mistake:
It is easy to mix up does and is.
No: Does he work here? Yes, he is.
Yes: Does he work here? Yes, he does.
The question has does, so the answer has does.
grammar.tip: Look at the first word. Say it again in the answer.
grammar.practice:
Write the short answer.
1. Do you speak English? Yes, ___.
2. Does Ben work at night? No, ___.
3. Do they live in a village? Yes, ___.
4. Does she know your name? Yes, ___.
5. Do you drive? No, ___.
6. Does the shop open on Sunday? No, ___.
7. Is he a farmer? Yes, ___.
8. Do Ana and Sam know the answer? Yes, ___.
grammar.answers:
1. I do  2. he doesn't  3. they do  4. she does  5. I don't  6. it doesn't  7. he is  8. they do
Wrong on 6? The shop is a thing: it. It goes with does.
Wrong on 7? The question has is, so the answer has is.

grammar.title: Two words in one: I'm, don't, doesn't, isn't
grammar.explanation:
Two words can make one short word.
One letter goes out.
A small mark goes in its place.
People say and write short forms a lot.
grammar.rule:
I am: I'm
do not: don't
does not: doesn't
is not: isn't
I am not: I'm not

I'm a student.
I don't live in a city.
She doesn't work on Sunday.
He isn't a doctor.
I'm not from a big city.
grammar.workedExample:
She does not live in a city. Make it short.
1. Find the two words: does not.
2. Take out the o in not.
3. Put the mark there: doesn't.
4. She doesn't live in a city.
grammar.mistake:
It is easy to write don't with he or she.
No: She don't live here.
Yes: She doesn't live here.
He, she and it go with does. So: doesn't.
grammar.tip: The mark goes in place of the letter: do not, don't.
grammar.practice:
Write the short form.
1. I am a student.
2. He does not drive.
3. We do not know.
4. It is not my bag.
5. She does not work here.
6. I do not live in a village.
7. Omar is not a farmer.
8. I am not a nurse.
grammar.answers:
1. I'm a student.  2. He doesn't drive.  3. We don't know.  4. It isn't my bag.  5. She doesn't work here.  6. I don't live in a village.  7. Omar isn't a farmer.  8. I'm not a nurse.
Wrong on 8? Am not has no short form. Write I'm not.
Check the mark: don't, not do'nt.

grammar.title: You for anyone: How do you spell that?
grammar.explanation:
Sometimes you means any person, not only you.
How do you spell that? It asks for the letters.
Use it to ask about words and things.
grammar.rule:
How do you spell that?
N-E-I-G-H-B-O-U-R.

How do you say this word?
Say it like this: SUR-name.

What do you call this in English?
It is a bottle.

Where do you wait for bus 6?
At the bus stop.

How do you write 12?
T-W-E-L-V-E.
grammar.workedExample:
You hear a new word: surname.
You want the letters.
1. You want to know how: How.
2. Then do, then you.
3. Then spell, then that.
4. How do you spell that?
5. The answer: S-U-R-N-A-M-E.
grammar.mistake:
It is easy to leave out do.
No: How you spell that?
Yes: How do you spell that?
No: What you call this?
Yes: What do you call this?
grammar.tip: A new word? Ask: How do you spell that?
grammar.practice:
Write the question. Start with the word in brackets.
1. You want the letters of a name. (How)
2. You want to say a new word. (How)
3. You want the English word for a thing. (What)
4. You want 15 as a word. (How)
5. You want the stop for bus 10. (Where)
6. The library has two doors. (Which)
grammar.answers:
1. How do you spell that?
2. How do you say this word?
3. What do you call this in English?
4. How do you write 15?
5. Where do you wait for bus 10?
6. Which door do you open?
Another which question with do you is fine too.
Wrong on any? Check for do before you.

readings.title: Meeting a Neighbour
readings.setting: Two neighbours meet on their street.
readings.passage:
Yara: Hello! I'm Yara. I live at number 5.
Ivan: Hello, Yara. I'm Ivan. Nice to meet you.
Yara: Nice to meet you. Do you live here?
Ivan: Yes, I do. I live at number 6, with my sister.
Yara: What is your job, Ivan?
Ivan: I'm a driver. I drive bus 10.
Yara: Does your sister work?
Ivan: No, she doesn't. She is a student.
Yara: I'm a nurse. I work at night.
Ivan: When do you sleep?
Yara: In the morning!

readings.title: Many Jobs, One Street
readings.passage:
People on one street do many jobs.
A doctor helps ill people. A nurse helps the doctor.
A driver drives a bus.
A farmer grows food. Many farmers live in a village.
A shopkeeper has a small shop.
A cleaner cleans offices and schools.
A police officer helps people on the street.
A teacher works at a school, and a student studies.
What about you? Do you work? Do you study?
Some people work and study.

readings.title: A Swimming Pool Card
readings.setting: The desk at a swimming pool.
readings.passage:
THE SWIMMING POOL — NEW CARD
Please write in capital letters.

First name: NADIA
Surname: DALE
Address: 14 PARK STREET
Phone number: 7 3 9 1 5 8
Job: NURSE

Which day do you swim? SATURDAY
When do you swim? 10 O'CLOCK

Thanks!

comprehension.q: Is Ivan a driver or a nurse?
comprehension.why: Ivan says: I'm a driver. I drive bus 10.

comprehension.q: Does Ivan live with his sister? Write a short answer.
comprehension.why: Ivan says: I live at number 6, with my sister.

comprehension.q: Yara lives at number 5. Ivan lives at number 6. What are they?
comprehension.why: They live on one street, next to each other. A neighbour lives next to you or near you.

comprehension.q: Why does Yara sleep in the morning?
comprehension.a: She works at night. She is a nurse.
comprehension.why: Yara says: I'm a nurse. I work at night.
Line 2: A nurse helps the doctor.

comprehension.q: Which word in the text means a person who studies?
You are on the street and you need help. Who do you ask?
comprehension.why: Line 7: A police officer helps people on the street.

comprehension.q: Nadia writes her surname on the form. What is it?
The person at the desk wants to call Nadia. Which line do they read?
comprehension.why: The form says: Phone number: 7 3 9 1 5 8. You call a person on that number.

comprehension.q: Does Nadia have a job? Write a short answer.
comprehension.a: Yes, she does. She is a nurse.

speaking.title: Speaking 1 — Do you, does she
speaking.instructions:
Listen. Say each question.
Do you live here?
Do they work on Monday?
Where do you work?
Does she live here?
Does he speak English?
Where does she work?
Tap the mic. Say the 6 questions.
Tap the mic again. Listen.
Check: do with you and they?
Does with he and she?
No s on the word after does?
speaking.tutor: Say the six questions to the tutor. Ask it to tell you any question with an s after does, like Where does she works?

speaking.title: Speaking 2 — Yes, I do. No, I don't.
speaking.instructions:
Read A. Say B.
1. A: Do you speak English? B: Yes, I do.
2. A: Do you live in a city? B: No, I don't.
3. A: Does your neighbour work? B: Yes, she does.
4. A: Does he drive a bus? B: No, he doesn't.
5. A: Is she a doctor? B: Yes, she is.
Tap the mic. Say the 5 B lines. Tap again. Listen.
Now answer 1 and 2 for you. Yes or no is fine.
Check: do or does in 1 to 4? Is in 5?
A friend can say A. No one with you? Say A and B.
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor to ask you eight do and does questions about your day. Answer each one with a short answer only, like No, I don't.

speaking.title: Speaking 3 — I'm, don't, doesn't, isn't
speaking.instructions:
Listen and repeat. First the two words, then the short form.
I am. I'm.
Do not. Don't.
Does not. Doesn't.
Is not. Isn't.
Now say these lines.
I'm a student.
I don't live in a city.
She doesn't work on Sunday.
He isn't a doctor.
Tap the mic. Say the 4 lines. Tap again. Listen.
Check: 4 lines?
Each short form is one fast word?
speaking.tutor: Say four sentences with I'm, don't, doesn't and isn't. They can be about you or a made-up person. Ask the tutor which short form it heard in each one.

speaking.title: Speaking 4 — About me
speaking.instructions:
Say 6 lines about you.
My name is ___. My surname is ___.
I'm a ___.
I work in ___. Or: I study at ___.
I live at ___.
I live in a city. Or: I live in a village.
I'm from ___.
You can use made-up details.
Say your job, or a job you know.
Tap the mic. Say it. Tap again. Listen.
Check: 6 lines? Your surname? A job word? City or village?
speaking.instructionsSpeech:

I live in a city. Or: I live in a village.

You can use made-up details.
Say your job, or a job you know.
Tap the mic. Say it. Tap again. Listen.
Check: 6 lines? Your surname? A job word? City or village?
speaking.tutor: Give the tutor your six made-up lines. Ask it to ask you three questions about them, and answer each with a full line.

speaking.title: Speaking 5 — At the desk
speaking.instructions:
You are at a desk. Listen to each question. Say your answer.
1. What is your first name?
2. What is your surname?
3. How do you spell that?
4. What is your address?
5. What is your phone number?
6. What is your job?
7. Do you live in a city?
Tap the mic. Say your 7 answers. Tap again. Listen.
Check with these:
My name is ___.
My surname is ___.
The letters, one at a time: D-A-L-E.
My address is ___.
My phone number is ___.
I'm a ___.
Yes, I do. Or: No, I don't.
You can use made-up details.
speaking.instructionsSpeech:

1. What is your first name?
2. What is your surname?
3. How do you spell that?
4. What is your address?

Yes, I do. Or: No, I don't.

speaking.title: Speaking 6 — Meet a new neighbour
speaking.instructions:
A new neighbour is at your door. You ask the questions.
You: Hello! I'm ___. What is your name?
Neighbour: I'm Tomas.
You: Sorry? How do you spell that?
Neighbour: T-O-M-A-S.
You: Nice to meet you, Tomas. What is your job?
Neighbour: I'm a farmer.
You: Where do you work?
Neighbour: In a village. Do you work?
You: Yes, I do. I'm a ___. Or: No, I don't. I'm a student.
Tap the mic. Say your 5 lines. Tap again. Listen.
Check: 4 questions from you? A short answer at the end?
A friend can say the Neighbour lines. No one with you? Read them, then say your lines.

speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor to be your new neighbour. Ask it five questions: its name, how you spell it, its job, where it works and when.

writing.title: Writing 1 — Questions for a new neighbour
writing.prompt:
Write 5 questions for a new neighbour.
Use do or does in each one.
writing.model:
Do you live at number 9?
Where do you work?
When do you work?
Does your sister live here?
Which shop do you like?
writing.criteria:
5 questions.
Do or does in each.
A capital letter at the start of each.
A question mark (?) at the end of each.
writing.support:
Copy the model.
In each question, change one word.
A number, a day or a person.
writing.extension: Write an answer to each question. Use Yes, I do or No, I don't where you can.

writing.title: Writing 2 — Yes or no?
writing.prompt:
Read the questions. Write a short answer for you.
Then write one more line after each one.
1. Do you live in a city?
2. Do you work at night?
3. Do you speak English?
4. Does your neighbour work?
5. Is your street big?
You can use made-up answers.
writing.model:
1. No, I don't. I live in a village.
2. No, I don't. I work in the morning.
3. Yes, I do. I'm a student of English.
4. Yes, she does. She is a cleaner.
5. No, it isn't. It is small.
writing.length: Five short answers and five lines
writing.criteria:
5 short answers, each with do, does or is.
5 more lines.
A short form in 3 lines: I'm, don't, doesn't or isn't.
A full stop (.) at the end of each.
writing.support:
Look at the first word of each question.
Do? Your answer has do or don't.
Does? It has does or doesn't.
Is? It has is or isn't.
writing.extension: Write two more questions about a friend with does. Answer them.

writing.title: Writing 3 — A person I know
writing.prompt:
Write 5 lines about a person you know.
A friend, a neighbour, or someone in your family.
Write the job and where they live.
Write one thing they don't do.
The person can be made up.
writing.model:
This is Mark. He is my neighbour.
He is a police officer.
He works at night.
He lives at number 3, in a small city.
He doesn't work on Sunday.
writing.criteria:
5 lines.
A job word in one line.
Works or lives, with an s, in 2 lines.
Doesn't or isn't in 1 line.
A capital letter and a full stop in each.
writing.support:
Use the model.
Change the name, the job and the number.
Keep he or she. Keep the s on works and lives.
writing.extension: Write 2 questions about the person with does. Answer them. Like this: Does Mark drive? No, he doesn't.

writing.title: Writing 4 — A form
writing.prompt:
Write a form like the one in Reading 3.
Add a line: City or village?
Write in capital letters.
You can use made-up details.
writing.model:
THE SWIMMING POOL — NEW CARD
First name: LEO
Surname: HART
Address: 3 GARDEN STREET
City or village? CITY
Phone number: 5 2 8 4 1 6
Job: STUDENT
Which day do you swim? TUESDAY
When do you swim? 6 O'CLOCK
writing.criteria:
9 lines, like the model.
All in capital letters.
The house number and the time as numbers.
writing.support:
Copy the form in Reading 3, line by line.
Change one line at a time.
For the job: your job, a job you know, or STUDENT.
writing.extension: Write two lines about your form: My surname is … I swim on …

activities.title: Practice 1 — Fix the question
activities.instructions:
Each question has one mistake. Write it right.
1. Where does she works?
2. Do he live here?
3. Does you speak English?
4. When do she study?
5. Where you live?
6. Does they know the answer?
7. Which day does he works?
8. Why do Omar study English?
activities.answers:
1. Where does she work?  2. Does he live here?  3. Do you speak English?  4. When does she study?  5. Where do you live?  6. Do they know the answer?  7. Which day does he work?  8. Why does Omar study English?
The s after does: 1 and 7.
Do and does swapped: 2, 3, 4, 6 and 8.
No do at all: 5.
7 or 8 right: good.
6 or less: read Pattern 1 and do it again.
activities.solo: Say each question out loud. Write it. Check with the key. Count the right ones.

activities.title: Practice 2 — Short answers
activities.instructions:
Write the short answer. Use the word in brackets.
1. Do you live here? (yes)
2. Does Tomas work at night? (no)
3. Do your neighbours know you? (yes)
4. Does the farmer live in a village? (yes)
5. Do you drive a bus? (no)
6. Is Priya a doctor? (no)
7. Does the shop open on Monday? (yes)
8. Do Eva and Leo study English? (no)
activities.answers:
1. Yes, I do.  2. No, he doesn't.  3. Yes, they do.  4. Yes, he does. Or: Yes, she does.  5. No, I don't.  6. No, she isn't.  7. Yes, it does.  8. No, they don't.
Number 6 starts with is, so the answer has isn't.
Number 4: a farmer can be a man or a woman. Both are right.
7 or 8 right: good.
6 or less: read Pattern 2 and do it again.
activities.solo: Say each answer out loud. Write it. Check with the key.

activities.title: Practice 3 — Make it short
activities.instructions:
Write each line with a short form: I'm, don't, doesn't or isn't.
1. I am from a small town.
2. She does not drive.
3. They do not live here.
4. He is not a teacher.
5. I do not know.
6. The shop is not open.
7. Omar does not work on Friday.
8. I am a cleaner.
activities.answers:
1. I'm from a small town.  2. She doesn't drive.  3. They don't live here.  4. He isn't a teacher.  5. I don't know.  6. The shop isn't open.  7. Omar doesn't work on Friday.  8. I'm a cleaner.
Check the mark in each. It goes in place of the letter. Not do'nt. Not does'nt.
7 or 8 right: good.
6 or less: read Pattern 3 and do it again.
activities.solo: Write each line. Read it out loud, fast. Check each mark with the key.

activities.title: Practice 4 — Match the question and the answer
activities.instructions:
Match 1 to 7 with a to g.
1. When do you work?
2. Why do you study English?
3. Which bus is it?
4. Where do you live?
5. What is your job?
6. What is your surname?
7. Do you know your neighbour?
a. For my job.
b. I'm a shopkeeper.
c. Yes, I do.
d. On Monday and Friday.
e. Bus 6.
f. At 9 Park Street.
g. It is Dale.
activities.answers:
1d  2a  3e  4f  5b  6g  7c
When: a time or a day. Why: a reason. Which: you choose.
6 or 7 right: good.
5 or less: read when, why and which on the Words page. Then do it again.
activities.solo: Read each question out loud. Say the answer. Check with the key.

activities.title: Practice 5 — Make the question
activities.instructions:
Make a question.
Start with a capital letter. End with a question mark.
1. spell / how / you / that / do
2. you / do / what / call / this
3. work / where / she / does
4. do / when / meet / they
5. live / you / here / do
6. say / do / this word / you / how
7. Omar / does / English / speak
activities.answers:
1. How do you spell that?
2. What do you call this?
3. Where does she work?
4. When do they meet?
5. Do you live here?
6. How do you say this word?
7. Does Omar speak English?
In 1, 2 and 6, you means any person.
6 or 7 right: good.
5 or less: read Patterns 1 and 4 and do it again.
activities.solo: Write each question. Read it out loud. Check with the key.

activities.title: Practice 6 — Which job is it?
activities.instructions:
Read. Write the job.
doctor, nurse, teacher, driver, farmer, student, shopkeeper, police officer, cleaner
1. I drive a bus. I'm a ___.
2. I help ill people. A nurse helps me. I'm a ___.
3. I have a small shop. I'm a ___.
4. I study English. I'm a ___.
5. I clean offices at night. I'm a ___.
6. I grow food in a village. I'm a ___.
7. I help people on the street. I'm a ___.
8. I work at a school. People study with me. I'm a ___.
9. I help ill people. I help the doctor. I'm a ___.
activities.answers:
1. driver  2. doctor  3. shopkeeper  4. student  5. cleaner  6. farmer  7. police officer  8. teacher  9. nurse
Numbers 2 and 9: a nurse helps the doctor.
8 or 9 right: good.
7 or less: say the Jobs words again. Then do it again.
activities.solo: Read each line out loud. Write the job. Check with the key.

quizzes.q: ___ your sister live in a city?
quizzes.why: Your sister is she, and she goes with does. Do is for I, you, we and they. Is and are do not go before live.
Does takes the s, so work has none. Where he works? has no does. He goes with does, not do.
The question starts with do, so the answer has do. I am answers a question with are. You do is about the other person. I speak needs more: I speak English.

quizzes.q: Does Omar work at night? No, ___.
quizzes.why: Omar is he, and he goes with does. He don't is wrong: don't is for I, you, we and they. Isn't answers a question with is. I don't is about you.
The question starts with is, so the answer has is. She does answers a does question. She do is wrong. Is she is a question, not an answer.

quizzes.q: She does not work on Sunday. Which is the short form?
quizzes.why: Take the o out of not and put the mark there: doesn't. Does'nt has the mark in the wrong place. She goes with does, not do. Isn't is is not, and it does not go with work.

quizzes.q: I am not a farmer. Which is the short form?
quizzes.why: I am makes I'm. Am not has no short form, so write I'm not. I don't needs a word like live or work. Im has no mark.

quizzes.q: You want the letters of a new word. What do you ask?
quizzes.why: How do you spell that? asks for the letters. You means any person here. How you spell that? has no do. Where asks for a place. How are you? asks about the person.
When asks for a time or a day: On Monday. In a shop answers where. For my job answers why. A driver answers What is your job?
Why asks for a reason: For my job. At night answers when. Yes, I do answers a do question. In a village answers where.

quizzes.q: I have a small shop. I work in it. I'm a ___.
quizzes.why: A shopkeeper has a shop and works in it. A farmer grows food. A police officer helps people on the street. A neighbour lives near you. It is not a job.

quizzes.q: It is your family name. Which word is it?
quizzes.why: Your surname is your family name, like Dale. Your address is a number and a street. A country is a big land. A number is a word like ten.

teacherNotes.note: Every card has a worked example before its practice, every exercise has a key with a score line, and every speaking task ends with record, listen back and a visible checklist. If you are helping, listen to the recordings together and point at the checklist rather than correcting mid-sentence.

teacherNotes.type: The one error worth your attention
teacherNotes.note: Where does she works? The s stays on the word after does. It is the commonest error with this pattern at any age, because the learner has just been told that he and she take an s. Point at does and ask where the s already is. It takes time to settle; Unit 14's routines give the same form much more practice.

Because is taught later in this level, so every answer to why here uses for (For my job) or a second sentence (He is a nurse). Both are natural English. Do not push for because yet, and accept either kind of answer.

Every task that asks for a name, surname, address, phone number, job or country says made-up details are fine, and a job task always offers a job you know or student. House numbers stay at 20 or below and phone numbers are said one number at a time, because 21 to 100 come in Unit 9. Never ask for real details and never correct a made-up one.

The AI tutor is a rehearsal partner, not a marking service, and no task is scored by it alone. Keep the made-up-details wording, and never ask the learner to give the tutor a real address or phone number.

selfAssessment.statement: I can ask: Do you live here? Where does she work?
I can answer: Yes, I do. No, she doesn't.
I can write I'm, don't, doesn't and isn't.
I can ask: How do you spell that?
I can answer when, why and which questions.
I can say my job and where I live.
I can find a job and an address on a form.
I can write my details on a form.

assignment.title: Meet a new neighbour
assignment.instructions:
Two parts.
1. Tap the mic. Say hello and your name. Spell your surname. Say your job, or a job you know, and where you live. Then ask 3 questions with do or does.
2. Write a form like Writing 4, in capital letters.
You can use made-up details.
assignment.submissionType: Audio recording and a written form
